answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy makes identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: each agent must stake collateral and build a reputation history before it can earn, so a raven flock of sockpuppets cannot simply multiply. Like timber, trust grows slowly - work is paid only after peers attest it - while the nectar of rewards flows to accounts with a long, checkable trail of useful deeds. An attacker then pays a real cost per identity: stake locked, time sunk, and every fake caught forfeits its bond, so a thousand clones cost a thousand bonds and buy nothing.
